title: pxGPT: a schema-constrained multimodal large language model framework for plant phenotyping
abstract: Summary Deep learning can scale image-based plant phenotyping but typically targets predefined traits, whereas manual phenotypic description is more flexible but difficult to scale. We present Phenotype eXplorer Generative Plant Traits (pxGPT), a Python framework that converts multi-view plant images into structured phenotype records. The workflow combines free-text description, dataset-specific schema generation with human review, and schema-constrained information extraction. We evaluated the extraction stage on three Brassica datasets using 78 973 annotations from 10 annotators who had no access to pxGPT predictions. For 38-45 qualitative traits per dataset, pxGPT-human agreement ranged from 0.572 to 0.712, compared with 0.620 to 0.739 agreement among human annotators. All 32 736 required trait fields were present; 93 values were empty, and no qualitative descriptor violations were recorded. For selected morphological structures, pooled false-positive rates were 0.5%-8.0%, while sensitivity varied across structure types in one mature-plant dataset (37.5%-100%). The curated schemas were applied unchanged with two commercial models and one locally hosted open-weight model, with differences in mean accuracy of 0.03 or less. In the evaluated Brassica datasets, these results support schema-guided extraction of visible plant traits without separate model training for each trait. Human-guided schema development offers a path to extend pxGPT to other crops and imaging conditions,

title: EasyIDP: A Python Package for Intermediate Data Processing in UAV-Based Plant Phenotyping
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and structure from motion (SfM) photogrammetry techniques are widely used for field-based, high-throughput plant phenotyping nowadays, but some of the intermediate processes throughout the workflow remain manual. For example, geographic information system (GIS) software is used to manually assess the 2D/3D field reconstruction quality and cropping region of interests (ROIs) from the whole field. In addition, extracting phenotypic traits from raw UAV images is more competitive than directly from the digital orthomosaic (DOM). Currently, no easy-to-use tools are available to implement previous tasks for commonly used commercial SfM software, such as Pix4D and Agisoft Metashape. Hence, an open source software package called easy intermediate data processor (EasyIDP; MIT license) was developed to decrease the workload in intermediate data processing mentioned above. The functions of the proposed package include (1) an ROI cropping module, assisting in reconstruction quality assessment and cropping ROIs from the whole field, and (2) an ROI reversing module, projecting ROIs to relative raw images. The result showed that both cropping and reversing modules work as expected. Moreover, the effects of ROI height selection and reversed ROI position on raw images to reverse calculation were discussed. This tool shows great potential for decreasing workload in data annotation for machine learning applications.

title: A Spatially Comprehensive Water Balance Model for Starch Potato from Combining Multispectral Ground Station and Remote Sensing Data in Precision Agriculture
abstract: The measurement of available water for agricultural plants is a crucial parameter for farmers, particularly to plan irrigation. However, an area-wide measurement is often not trivial as there are several inputs and outputs of water into the system. Here, we present a high-resolution, remote sensing-based water balance model for starch potato cultivation, combining multispectral ground station data with UAV and satellite imagery. Over a three-year period (2021–2023), data from Arable Mark 2 ground stations, DJI Phantom 4 MS drones, PlanetScope satellites, and Sentinel-2 satellites were collected in Mecklenburg–Western Pomerania, Germany. The model utilizes NDVI-based crop coefficients (R2 = 0.999) to estimate evapotranspiration and integrates on-farm irrigation and precipitation data for precise water balance calculations. A correlation with reference NDVI observations by Arable Mark 2 systems can be shown for UAV (R2 = 0.94), PlanetScope satellite data (R2 = 0.94), and Sentinel-2 satellite data (R2 = 0.93). We demonstrate the model’s ability to capture intra-site heterogeneity on a precision farming scale. Our spatially comprehensive model enables farmers to optimize irrigation strategies, reducing water and energy use. Although the results are based on sprinkler irrigation, the model remains adaptable for advanced irrigation methods such as drip and subsurface systems.

Transfer learning between crop types for semantic segmentation of crops versus weeds in precision agriculture
abstract:
Abstract 
                   Agricultural robots rely on semantic segmentation for distinguishing between crops and weeds to perform selective treatments and increase yield and crop health while reducing the amount of chemicals used. Deep‐learning approaches have recently achieved both excellent classification performance and real‐time execution. However, these techniques also rely on a large amount of training data, requiring a substantial labeling effort, both of which are scarce in precision agriculture. Additional design efforts are required to achieve commercially viable performance levels under varying environmental conditions and crop growth stages. In this paper, we explore the role of knowledge transfer between deep‐learning‐based classifiers for different crop types, with the goal of reducing the retraining time and labeling efforts required for a new crop. We examine the classification performance on three datasets with different crop types and containing a variety of weeds and compare the performance and retraining efforts required when using data labeled at pixel level with partially labeled data obtained through a less time‐consuming procedure of annotating the segmentation output. We show that transfer learning between different crop types is possible and reduces training times for up to 80%. title: MTS-CNN: Multi-task semantic segmentation-convolutional neural network for detecting crops and weeds
abstract: Research is being extensively conducted on using deep learning in the field of crop and weed segmentation based on images captured with a camera. However, the segmentation performance for various crops and weeds varies significantly, implying that certain classes of crops or weeds are not being detected properly. This problem may also occur in the loss calculations used in crop and weed segmentation. In previous studies, the cross-entropy loss (corresponding to a distribution loss) and dice loss (using spatial information) have been widely used. However, such losses lead to large discrepancies in crop and weed segmentation performance, as the correlations between crop and weed classes are not considered. In order to solve these problems, this study proposes multi-task semantic segmentation-convolutional neural network for detecting crops and weeds (MTS-CNN) using one-stage training. This approach adds the crop, weed, and both (crop and weed) losses to heighten the correlations between the crop and weed classes, and designs the model so that the object (crop and weed) region is trained intensively. In experiments conducted using three types of open databases - the BoniRob dataset, a crop/weed field image dataset (CWFID), and rice seedling and weed dataset - the mean intersection of union (MIOU) values of the segmentation for the crops and weeds in the MTS-CNN are 0.9164, 0.8372, and 0.8260, respectively. Training instance segmentation neural network with synthetic datasets for crop seed phenotyping
abstract: In order to train the neural network for plant phenotyping, a sufficient amount of training data must be prepared, which requires time-consuming manual data annotation process that often becomes the limiting step. Here, we show that an instance segmentation neural network aimed to phenotype the barley seed morphology of various cultivars, can be sufficiently trained purely by a synthetically generated dataset. Our attempt is based on the concept of domain randomization, where a large amount of image is generated by randomly orienting the seed object to a virtual canvas. The trained model showed 96% recall and 95% average Precision against the real-world test dataset. We show that our approach is effective also for various crops including rice, lettuce, oat, and wheat. Constructing and utilizing such synthetic data can be a powerful method to alleviate human labor costs for deploying deep learning-based analysis in the agricultural domain.

Prediction of cotton yield based on soil texture, weather conditions and UAV imagery using deep learning
abstract: Crop yield prediction is important for farmers to conduct proper field management and make marketing decisions. Yield prediction models built on single-type and same-year data may not reflect the holistic effect of environment and management on crop development. This study aimed to quantify cotton yield variation due to soil texture and weather conditions using the multiple-year unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and deep learning techniques. UAV images were collected about once a month to quantify cotton growth at two irrigated cotton fields in three years (2017–2019). Soil apparent electrical conductivity (ECₐ) of the fields was measured and calibrated to quantify soil texture and soil water holding capacity using eleven soil features. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were used to process and analyse the soil features in seven different depths. Similarly, a second CNN was used to analyse the six weather parameters derived from the historical data of a nearby weather station. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) network was used to predict cotton yield using the processed soil data, weather data, and UAV-based image features (e.g., NDVI) of different months. Results show that the GRU model trained with data in two years could predict the cotton yield in a third year with prediction errors of mean average error from 247 (8.9%) to 384 kg ha⁻¹ (13.7%). The study indicates that the developed CNN and GRU networks have the potential to predict crop yield of years other than the one

title: An Automated Framework for Plant Detection Based on Deep Simulated Learning from Drone Imagery
abstract: Traditional mapping and monitoring of agricultural fields are expensive, laborious, and may contain human errors. Technological advances in platforms and sensors, followed by artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) breakthroughs in intelligent data processing, led to improving the remote sensing applications for precision agriculture (PA). Therefore, technological advances in platforms and sensors and intelligent data processing methods, such as machine learning and DL, and geospatial and remote sensing technologies, have improved the quality of agricultural land monitoring for PA needs. However, providing ground truth data for model training is a time-consuming and tedious task and may contain multiple human errors. This paper proposes an automated and fully unsupervised framework based on image processing and DL methods for plant detection in agricultural lands from very high-resolution drone remote sensing imagery. The proposed framework’s main idea is to automatically generate an unlimited amount of simulated training data from the input image. This capability is advantageous for DL methods and can solve their biggest drawback, i.e., requiring a considerable amount of training data. This framework’s core is based on the faster regional convolutional neural network (R-CNN) with the backbone of ResNet-101 for object detection. The proposed framework’s efficiency was evaluated by two different image sets from two cornfields, acquired by an RGB camera mounted on

title: BPFun: a deep learning framework for bioactive peptide function prediction using multi-label strategy by transformer-driven and sequence rich intrinsic information
abstract: Bioactive peptides are beneficial or have physiological effects on the life activities of biological organisms. The functions of bioactive peptides are diverse, usually with one or more, so accurately detecting the multiple functions of multi-functional peptides is extremely important. Traditional experimental identification methods are time-consuming, laborious and costly. To overcome these problems, we adopt a computational biology approach and propose a new model BPFun based on deep learning, which can predict seven functions including anticancer, antibacterial, antihypertensive and so on. In BPFun, we obtained the features of bioactive peptides from different aspects, including biological and physicochemical features. Meanwhile, adopting data augmentation to solve the problem of data imbalance. We combine convolutional networks of different scales and Bi-LSTM layers to obtain high-level feature vectors of different features. Finally, the prediction performance is improved by combining these fused features and combining the self-attention mechanism and the Bi-LSTM layer. Our experiments show that BPFun based on five types of sequence features significantly improves the prediction performance of bioactive peptides. Experiments on the test dataset showed that BPFun gets the accuracy and absolute truth value of 0.6577 and 0.6573 on the dataset of seven functional classifications and was superior to other methods. Codes and data are available at https://github.com/291357657/BP

RAGP: a retrieval-augmented deep learning model for genomic prediction in crop breeding.
abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) plays a pivotal role in expediting genetic gains for crop breeding. Recently, deep learning models has attracted growing attention in this field due to its superior performance over traditional models. However, most advanced models rely on simplified numerical representations of genomic variants and treat individuals in isolation, failing to capture the full complexity of genetic variation and the genetic relatedness among individuals. In response, we propose RAGP, a deep learning model driven by a retrieval-augmented mechanism composed of two synergistic components: (1) an embedding-based retrieval module that identifies a group of nearest neighbors highly relevant to the target sample as references, employs a phenotype-aware encoder to refine the representation space and capture informative genetic structures; (2) an augmentation module that integrates the retrieved references to enhance the target representation. The enriched representation is then propagated through a regression network for final prediction. This retrieval-guided strategy enables more informed and fine-grained utilization of genomic data and strengthens the model's capacity to capture individual-level genetic relationships. Extensive experiments reveal that RAGP achieves consistently superior predictive performance compared to both conventional methods and state-of-the-art deep learning models. By incorporating retrieval-augmented mechanisms, RAGP achieves substantial improvements

title: Synthetic meets authentic (Part II): Field-imaging-free auto-annotation and multi-orchard field validation for apple detection and segmentation
IrrMapper: A Machine Learning Approach for High Resolution Mapping of Irrigated Agriculture Across the Western U.S.
abstract: High frequency and spatially explicit irrigated land maps are important for understanding the patterns and impacts of consumptive water use by agriculture. We built annual, 30 m resolution irrigation maps using Google Earth Engine for the years 1986–2018 for 11 western states within the conterminous U.S. Our map classifies lands into four classes: irrigated agriculture, dryland agriculture, uncultivated land, and wetlands. We built an extensive geospatial database of land cover from each class, including over 50,000 human-verified irrigated fields, 38,000 dryland fields, and over 500,000 km     2     of uncultivated lands. We used 60,000 point samples from 28 years to extract Landsat satellite imagery, as well as climate, meteorology, and terrain data to train a Random Forest classifier. Using a spatially independent validation dataset of 40,000 points, we found our classifier has an overall binary classification (irrigated vs. unirrigated) accuracy of 97.8%, and a four-class overall accuracy of 90.8%. We compared our results to Census of Agriculture irrigation estimates over the seven years of available data and found good overall agreement between the 2832 county-level estimates (r     2     = 0.90), and high agreement when estimates are aggregated to the state level (r     2     = 0.94). We analyzed trends over the 33-year study period, finding an increase of 15% (15,000 km     2    ) in irrigated area in our study region. We found notable decreases in irrigated area in de

title: Applying RGB- and Thermal-Based Vegetation Indices from UAVs for High-Throughput Field Phenotyping of Drought Tolerance in Forage Grasses
abstract: The persistence and productivity of forage grasses, important sources for feed production, are threatened by climate change-induced drought. Breeding programs are in search of new drought tolerant forage grass varieties, but those programs still rely on time-consuming and less consistent visual scoring by breeders. In this study, we evaluate whether Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) based remote sensing can complement or replace this visual breeder score. A field experiment was set up to test the drought tolerance of genotypes from three common forage types of two different species: Festuca arundinacea, diploid Lolium perenne and tetraploid Lolium perenne. Drought stress was imposed by using mobile rainout shelters. UAV flights with RGB and thermal sensors were conducted at five time points during the experiment. Visual-based indices from different colour spaces were selected that were closely correlated to the breeder score. Furthermore, several indices, in particular H and NDLab, from the HSV (Hue Saturation Value) and CIELab (Commission Internationale de l’éclairage) colour space, respectively, displayed a broad-sense heritability that was as high or higher than the visual breeder score, making these indices highly suited for high-throughput field phenotyping applications that can complement or even replace the breeder score. The thermal-based Crop Water Stress Index CWSI provided complementary information to visual-based indices, enabling the analysis of differences in ecophy

title: Machine Learning Models in Precision Agriculture for Classification of Diseases
abstract: The bond between machine learning models and the agriculture field is becoming stronger with each passing day. The pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, VggNet, and GoogleNet models commonly support various tasks in the precision agriculture field, such as disease detection, nitrogen status estimation, leaf area index identification, nutrient status measuring, finding pesticide requirements, measuring growth, etc. These tasks involve a huge amount of data, such as simple cell phone images, satellite imagery data, vegetation index data, images from UAVs, and sensor data from various soil and water sensors. Analyzing and finding insight from such data is a complex task. In this article, a framework is proposed using the transfer learning method for disease classification using manual CNN model along with the pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, and GoogleNet. The 5450-image dataset,, is considered that includes four wheat disease labels and a healthy wheat label, is used, which was constructed from publicly available datasets. The fine-tuned models are compared for the disease prediction task using the parameters such as accuracy, F1 score, recall and precision. Transfer learning ResNet50 gives promising results once fine-tuned, having the accuracy of 93% compared with other transfer learning models, which ranges from 61 % to 78%. The framework proposed can identify diseases for various crops in agriculture field.
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: RTM-KDOS: Keypoint detection and operability scoring for multifunctional tomato harvesting and de-leafing robots
SPGrowing: an unsupervised individual plant segmentation pipeline from UAV-derived point clouds for high-throughput in-field maize phenotyping
abstract: In-field plant phenotyping is essential for understanding gene–environment interactions and supporting crop breeding. While unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based photogrammetry enables high-throughput three-dimensional (3D) sensing, accurate plant-level analysis of densely planted crops like maize remains challenging due to morphological complexity, leaf occlusion, and dynamic canopy structures. To address these issues, this study develops an end-to-end phenotyping pipeline based on UAV-derived point clouds, incorporating cross-circling oblique (CCO) flight sampling, point cloud reconstruction and preprocessing, individual plant segmentation, and trait extraction, which is applied to multiple maize varieties (ZD 958, SKT 1506, SBR), growth stages (V3–R2), and planting spacings (0.4–0.8 m). At the core of the pipeline, an unsupervised individual plant segmentation algorithm (SPGrowing) is proposed, which integrates stem core detection via ground-projected density analysis, superpoint-based structural abstraction for efficient homogeneous partition representation, and multi-source shortest-path optimization incorporating stem-centered growth patterns as topological constraints. Validation results showed that SPGrowing consistently outperformed existing segmentation benchmarks, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) of 0.950 and a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 0.898 at the point level, and an AP 50 of 0.949 at the object level. The extracted plant-level traits closely matched

title: UAV-Based Computer Vision for Cattle Detection and Feed Bunk Spatial Analysis
abstract: Beef cattle production is central to Brazilian agribusiness and faces growing demands for efficiency, sustainability, and animal welfare. Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) offers tools to address these challenges, particularly through monitoring feeding-related spatial patterns in confined systems. Feeding management plays a decisive role in animal performance, yet its evaluation still relies largely on subjective, labor-intensive visual inspections that are hard to scale and prone to bias. This work proposes a computer vision framework based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) to quantify cattle alignment and spatial dispersion at the feed bunk under real-world feedlot conditions. A UAV dataset was collected during flight campaigns at a commercial feedlot in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil. Images were manually annotated into cattle head and cattle back classes to support object detection and image-level spatial analysis of cattle distribution. You Only Look Once (YOLO) models, namely YOLOv8 and YOLOv11, were evaluated, with YOLOv8 small used for the downstream spatial analysis. The feed bunk region was segmented using the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and geometric metrics based on detected head positions were developed to characterize alignment, spacing regularity, and clustering. The selected detector achieved 84.30% mAP50 and 35.50% mAP50-95, with an inference time of approximately 2.7 ms per image on an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti GPU. The resulting metrics distinguished representativ

title: Rail-Guided IoT Imaging System for Leaf-Level Monitoring in Small-Scale Citrus Plots
abstract: This paper presents a rail-guided IoT imaging system designed to overcome the difficulty of obtaining consistent, leaf-level citrus images for long-term agricultural monitoring by combining deterministic electromechanical positioning, embedded control, edge computing, and cloud-based data management. It incorporates a cable-suspended linear actuation mechanism together with two inclined cameras, motion control based on ESP32 microcontrollers, a Raspberry Pi 5 for processing, and AWS S3 for cloud services to automate the processes of image acquisition, synchronization, storage, and remote visualization. By limiting image capture to a fixed and repeatable path, the platform reduces the variation in viewpoint that is typically found with aerial and ground-mobile robots, thus allowing the systematic production of consistent image datasets for use in plant phenotyping and pest monitoring. The system was implemented and tested in a citrus orchard under real-world operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate the system's autonomous and stable operation, reliable image acquisition, continuous synchronization with the cloud and repeatable monitoring over long periods of time with a low-cost hardware design suitable for research-scale setups. The platform provides a reproducible embedded imaging setup, which improves the consistency of agricultural image acquisition and enables the development and evaluation of computer vision algorithms for precision agriculture.
venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

title: DaYa-YOLO: Substituting a Frozen Colorimetric Prior for Learned Attention in Edge-deployed Rice Pest and Disease Detection
abstract: Rice pest detection must run on affordable handheld hardware, yet color space and edge deployability have been studied separately.We ask whether a frozen color prior can replace learned attention.DaYa-YOLO pairs an RGB backbone with a frozen sRGB to CIELAB transform and a trainable scaling layer, compared against three attention modules over five seeds on 13 field-collected rice classes.DaYa-LAB reaches 0.707 mean mAP50 against the YOLO11 baseline's 0.709, and none of the eleven architectures separates on mean accuracy, though the dual-branch and single-branch architectures differ in neck wiring, so this is accuracy parity rather than controlled substitution.An architecture-matched control without the color transform reaches 0.705 and is equally indistinguishable, so the transform adds no measurable accuracy.Robustness falls for every dual-branch model.Deployment separates them: 8 of 10 produced a working Jetson Nano engine.Reproducible latency and compilation are practical deployment criteria.
venue: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems

title: Boundary-weighted supervision and multi-scale context enhancement for greenhouse tomato instance segmentation using YOLO11n-seg
abstract: Accurate tomato instance segmentation in greenhouse scenes remains challenging because of fruit occlusion, instance contact, ambiguous boundaries, and the visual similarity between green fruits and leaves. This study presents a lightweight YOLO11n-seg framework that combines a morphology-based shape-boundary-driven (SBD) weighting strategy with the previously proposed CMPRD multi-scale context module. SBD constructs a narrow contour band for each ground-truth instance and increases the contribution of boundary pixels to the mask loss during training without altering the inference graph, whereas CMPRD replaces SPPF near the end of the YOLO11n-seg backbone to enhance multi-scale contextual representation. Across five independent runs on the 128-image validation split (mean ± standard deviation), the combined model increases Mask Recall from \(0.7656\pm 0.0046\) to \(0.7726\pm 0.0039\) and Mask mAP50–95 from \(0.6587\pm 0.0025\) to \(0.6812\pm 0.0026\) relative to YOLO11n-seg, while Mask Precision changes from \(0.7989\pm 0.0037\) to \(0.7961\pm 0.0035\) . In the fixed seed-0 comparison with additional baselines, the larger YOLOv8s-seg and YOLO11s-seg models achieve Mask mAP50–95 values of 0.69161 and 0.69434, respectively, whereas a literature-guided reimplementation of Enhanced YOLO11n-Seg achieves 0.67840 under a comparable lightweight computational budget. On the untouched 161-image official test set, the primary Mask mAP50–95 results, reported as the mean ± standard deviati

title: ICVDD-5: A Real-Field Multi-Crop Dataset and CNN–Transformer Ensemble for Disease Recognition, Severity Estimation and Farmer Advisory
abstract: In smart agriculture, deterioration of vegetable quality due to crop diseases is an issue that poses a threat to food security. Manual inspection is subjective and laboratory testing is time consuming and expensive, unless early detection is possible to take preventive measures and to minimize losses. In this study, Indian Crop Visual Disease Dataset-5 (ICVDD-5) was developed, and an AI-based decision support system for real-field multi-crop disease recognition, severity assessment and farmer guidance was developed. A total of 6,376 images (880 original healthy and diseased field images from five vegetable crops (brinjal, cabbage, chilli, okra and tomato) across 21 classes) were used as the training set in the augmentation process in ICVDD-5. The hybrid ensemble integrates a tuned custom CNN for local features related to symptoms with the pretrained Vision Transformer for global relationships. On the held-out test set, the ensemble achieved 91.84% accuracy, 93.11% precision, 91.02% recall, and a 92.05% F1 score. A class-specific severity estimator not only classifies tissue but also assigns it an ordinal grade for symptomatic tissue. A rule-based decision module is then used to integrate predicted disease, disease group spread risk, model confidence, and disease severity to prioritize interventions and provide crop specific management recommendations. Low-confidence predictions are not made, and are referred for recapture or expert review, before treatment advice is given. Th

title: AgriSense AI: An Integrated Dual-Engine Deep Transfer Learning and Ensemble Regression Framework for Crop Foliar Disease Diagnosis and Agricultural Commodity Price Forecasting
abstract: Abstract— Agricultural productivity and rural economic stability in developing agrarian economies face dual systemic vulnerabilities: unmitigated phytopathological outbreaks and severe market price volatility. This paper presents AgriSense AI, an end-to-end, dual-engine decision-support framework that integrates convolutional transfer learning for automated foliar disease diagnosis with non-linear ensemble regression for regional commodity price forecasting. A computer vision pipeline is constructed over a 15-class subset of the PlantVillage dataset using FastAI and a pre-trained ResNet-18 architecture (128x128 spatial normalization), achieving a validation accuracy of 99.95% (loss: 0.001528) and a macro-averaged Precision, Recall, and F1-Score of 0.9996. Second, a leakage-free econometric pricing engine is developed over Indian agricultural market records (N = 2,794 across 17 encoded features), where a 100-estimator Random Forest Regressor achieves an out-of-sample RMSE of 2,659.49 INR, MAE of 1,450.25 INR, and R2 of 0.7200. Both serialized engines are unified within a production Streamlit web application. venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Multi-crop disease classification using a Dilateformer-MobileNetV2 dual-branch fusion network
abstract: Multi-crop disease classification requires discrimination among visually similar symptoms. This study evaluates late feature fusion of Dilateformer and MobileNetV2 for 45-class image classification. The two pooled representations are concatenated before classification. The original experiment achieved 97.21% Top-1 accuracy and 96.63% macro F1 on a 59,905-image benchmark. During revision, PlantDoc-derived samples were added to the existing collection to broaden image diversity. On this expanded 68,682-sample dataset, the selected fusion checkpoint achieved 95.45% accuracy and 93.63% macro F1 on 6,550 test samples, compared with 95.48% accuracy for MobileNetV2. These results belong to distinct data and implementation versions. Dataset provenance, parameter accounting and branch-specific gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) support interpretation of the revision-stage results. The findings demonstrate useful multi-crop classification performance, while showing that simple feature concatenation does not guarantee improvement over a single branch. Independent field generalization remains to be established.

title: Areca-CEDNet: Arecanut Plant Disease Classification Using Convolutional Encoder–decoder Network
abstract: Plant disease classification is crucial in agriculture for ensuring food security and sustainability.Traditional methods require expert knowledge, are time-consuming, and does not appropriate for large-scale analysis.Deep Learning (DL)-assisted image classification techniques offer effective performance in identifying plant diseases.This research proposes the arecanut leaf disease classification approach called Areca-Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Network (Areca-CEDNet) architecture, which builds on and extends the concepts of the CED-Net and the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN).The study uses two datasets: a private Arecanut and the publicly available PlantVillage dataset, for implementing the proposed approach.A Visual Geometric Group-16 (VGG16) architecture extracts both low-and high-level features.Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Areca-CEDNet method achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.93% on Arecanut dataset and 99.65% on PlantVillage dataset.This approach makes a significant contribution to sustainable Artificial Intelligence (AI) for plant disease detection by improving model generalization and allowing precise classification over diverse classes with smaller image sizes in DL-based agricultural applications.
venue: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems

title: Dataset: Morphological traits, yield, and RGB images of Mung Bean (Vigna radiata L.) subjected to biofertilization
abstract: Mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) is a highly nutritious and sustainable pulse crop essential for global food security, yet its production is increasingly constrained by environmental and biotic stresses. To address these challenges through advanced crop management and precision agriculture, this paper presents a comprehensive agronomic and image dataset of mung bean plants subjected to biofertilization. The dataset encompasses detailed quantitative measurements of key morphophysiological and productive traits—including plant height, stem diameter, nodule and biomass weight, grain yield, and relative chlorophyll content—collected 60 days after planting across 18 experimental units. Crucially, these traditional biometric records are paired with high-resolution (24.2-megapixel) RGB images captured under standardized artificial night lighting and a controlled dark backdrop to perfectly isolate plant architecture. By integrating destructive agronomic evaluations with standardized visual data, this dataset provides a fundamental resource for researchers. It directly enables the development and validation of computer vision algorithms, machine learning models, and non-invasive phenotyping tools designed to assess biofertilizer efficacy and optimize crop yields in sustainable agricultural systems.
venue: Trends in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences.

title: Classification algorithms for selecting crop types in Asian countries based on soil and climate parameters
abstract: Classifying crops from environmental conditions can support agricultural data exploration, but an observed crop is not necessarily the most suitable crop for that land. We compare multinomial logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors (kNN), and random forest on a transparent seven-country South Asian grid benchmark. Crop-area and surface-soil layers came from the open ACASA 50 km collection; annual mean temperature and precipitation were sampled from WorldClim 2.1 climate normals. For each grid cell, the largest of 12 crop-area layers defined the observed dominant-crop label. Cells without mapped crops, incomplete inputs, or less than 50% dominance were removed, and classes with fewer than 30 records were excluded, leaving 1,070 cells in seven crop classes. No crop-area layer was used as a predictor. Disjoint 2° spatial blocks supplied 642 training, 215 validation, and 213 test cells. On the held-out test blocks, kNN achieved 73.7% accuracy and 0.461 macro-F1, versus 70.9% and 0.441 for random forest and 70.0% and 0.398 for logistic regression. Its advantage over random forest in accuracy was 2.8 percentage points, but a paired block-bootstrap interval crossed zero. Leave-one-country-out tests were markedly less reliable, especially in Afghanistan and Pakistan. The results identify a modestly stronger within-region classifier for mapped crop dominance under this protocol; they do not validate agronomic suitability, yield benefit, or transfer to new countries.

title: FedXCrop: Privacy-Preserving Crop Disease Detection via Federated Learning with Post-Aggregation Explainability under Non-IID Farm Distributions
abstract: Deep learning can classify crop diseases accurately from benchmark leaf images, but centralized training requires farms to share raw data, and predictions without explanations offer limited support for treatment decisions. We present FedXCrop, a federated crop disease classification pipeline that quantitatively evaluates explanations of the aggregated global model. A MobileNetV2 model trained centrally on PlantVillage achieved 99.38% test accuracy (standard deviation 0.05 over three seeds) on a fixed test set of 5,428 images across 38 classes. Federated models initialized with ImageNet weights were trained for 30 rounds across five clients. FedAvg achieved 98.81% accuracy with identically distributed clients and 98.81%, 98.59%, and 97.78% under Dirichlet label skew (alpha = 1, 0.5, and 0.1, respectively). FedProx was not significantly different from FedAvg at any heterogeneity level (McNemar p > 0.3). Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad explanations were evaluated on 380 test images. Both attributed more energy to the leaf than chance (0.70-0.78 versus 0.60), while Grad-CAM maps from federated and centralized models showed Spearman correlations of 0.74-0.76. Agreement decreased as heterogeneity increased, lesion localization was only modestly above chance, and a model-randomization test indicated that SmoothGrad maps depended substantially on image structure rather than learned parameters. In this setting, label skew reduced federated accuracy by 0.6-1.6 percentage points relative to cen

title: Classification of rice varieties using RGB images integrated with image-derived geometric traits based on deep learning models
abstract: Deep learning (DL) offers a promising approach for accurate, scalable plant classification. However, most DL studies on rice depend on seed images. In this study, we assessed leaf-based classification of nine rice varieties using red, green, and blue (RGB) images and geometric traits derived from these images at the vegetative stage, creating an image-guided feature integration model. The classification strategies included traits-based, RGB image-based, and combined RGB image and traits-based methods. For geometric trait measurements, six traits were calculated with the OpenCV module in Python. Classification was conducted at six growth stages: 13, 21, 23, 29, 33, and 35 days after sowing (DAS). Traits-based classification was performed using random forest and support vector machine models. For RGB image-only classification and RGB images combined with trait classification, four convolutional neural networks (CNNs): EfficientNetV2, InceptionV3, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50 were evaluated along with an Ensemble model of ResNet and EfficientNet. Traits-based classification achieved less than 0.5 accuracy at all stages. For RGB image-based evaluation, EfficientNetV2, ResNet-50, and ConvNeXt-Tiny gave an accuracy of 0.76 at 29 DAS, with the lowest being 0.43 for InceptionV3 at 13 and 23 DAS, and the highest 0.80 for Ensemble at 29 DAS. Similarly, for the trait integration method, the Ensemble model achieved the highest accuracy, 0.82, at 29 DAS. The highest-misclassified varietie

title: PLANTEUR: A Crop-Type Segmentation Benchmark for Tropical Regions
abstract: We introduce PLANTEUR, a benchmark for crop-type mapping from satellite images in the French overseas territories. Building on the PASTIS design, PLANTEUR provides georeferenced and aligned Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1, and Landsat-8 sequences with parcel-derived labels spanning six tropical regions and an 8-class label space. We define both a standard test split and a leave-one-island-out protocol to measure cross-territory generalization, and evaluate fully supervised models, linear probes, and fine-tuned foundation models. The benchmark code and data are open source and available on GitHub and Hugging Face.

title: Security-aware selective quantization and optimization framework (SASQOF) for resource-constrained ML-based IoT irrigation systems
abstract: This study evaluates selective dynamic 8-bit integer (INT8) quantization of long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent weights while retaining a 32-bit floating-point (FP32) linear output layer, together with authenticated sensor processing, using 10,257 observations from the Secured and Optimized IoT-Based Irrigation System (SOIBIS) experimental farm at Federal University Lokoja, Nigeria. Five seeded runs compare eight models under chronological and feature-group evaluations. The chronological test contains only label pattern 101, for which a majority baseline also achieves 100% exact-match accuracy. On the class-diverse feature-group test, selective quantization achieves 98.40% mean exact-match accuracy, compared with 100% for a decision tree and 84.68% for a majority baseline. Selective quantization reduces serialized model size by 64.9% and single-record host model-only latency by 50.7%, but increases 12-record model-only latency by approximately 41.1%. Mean authenticated single-record inference-path time is 0.441 ms on the host. All 1,200 specified functional packet checks met their expected outcomes. These are host-software findings, not evidence of ESP32 deployment, independently verified pump actuation, water savings, or agronomic superiority.

title: Benchmarking Intent Classification in Extremely Low-Resource Indo-Aryan Dialects: An Empirical Study on Dhatki Agricultural Telemetry
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) models achieve state-of-the-art benchmarks in high-resource global languages, yet regional vernacular dialects spoken by millions of marginalized pastoralists remain entirely excluded from digital conversational interfaces. Dhatki, an Indo-Aryan transitional language spoken by over 2.5 million inhabitants across the Thar Desert of southeastern Sindh, Pakistan, lacks standardized tokenizers, orthographic corpora, and annotated evaluation benchmarks. In this technical report, we introduce the first domain-specific, curated Intent Classification Dataset for Dhatki agricultural telemetry (comprising 1,000 verified acoustic and textual utterances spanning 10 operational agricultural classes, hosted openly on Hugging Face). We empirically benchmark baseline lexical models against multilingual transformer representations (mBERT, IndicBERT, XLM-RoBERTa, and a proposed domain-specific Dhatki-DistilBERT) under severe resource constraints. Our experimental findings demonstrate that custom subword Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tuned to phonetic Dhatki transcriptions achieves a Micro-F1 score of 89.4% with an edge latency of 14.2 ms, proving the viability of low-latency, offline voice interfaces for low-resource desert agriculture. Open-Access Resources: • Hugging Face Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lokeshsonara/dhatki-agri-intents • Live Research Portal: https://agri-idas.tech/
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: A physics-regularized recurrent neural network for thermal sterilization of canned solid–liquid foods
Integrating physicochemical properties into an augmented 3D molecular learning framework for taste prediction
abstract: Taste is a crucial sensory modality that shapes human survival and health, and sweetness and bitterness in particular are key properties that require early stage assessment in food and pharmaceutical development. In this study, we propose a deep learning based framework for taste prediction that integrates computationally generated three-dimensional (3D) molecular conformers with physicochemical properties, and we establish a multi-class classification scheme that also encompasses tasteless compounds. The model learns structural information from 3D molecular representations generated from SMILES, while physicochemical descriptors are incorporated as conditional inputs to modulate the learned structural embeddings. We evaluated binary (sweet vs. bitter) and three-class (sweet, bitter, and tasteless) classification tasks, including compounds reported as tasteless. To prevent molecule-level leakage, we adopt a splitting strategy that avoids redundancy across subsets, and to mitigate class imbalance especially for the tasteless class we introduce 3D-based data augmentation to enhance structural diversity. Performance was evaluated using standard classification metrics along with uncertainty estimation. Overall, the physicochemically conditioned model showed more stable and improved predictive performance compared with a 3D-only baseline. To situate this improvement relative to conventional cheminformatics approaches, we additionally benchmarked an extended version of the model ag

title: A muzzle-based self-enhancing cow recognition method using YOLO and LLM
abstract: In the modern era, using the technology of image processing, people are being facilitated in many sectors. Therefore, we have decided to do research on cow recognition using the methods of image processing. Because cows are pretty essential for human beings, and people from the entire world are being facilitated by cows. Because of that reason, many technologies have been invented till now for the cow. Here we have presented an approach to identify the cow. Like the fingerprint of a human, the cow muzzle is also unique. Due to this reason, we can recognize the cow based on the muzzle. To recognize muzzles, we have used Yolo and the Structural Similarity Index (SSI). Image processing is a sector of Artificial Intelligence and data is quite important to train models. Moreover, to train a model for image processing, it is needed to manage a high-configuration computer. But there are many regions in the world where people hardly get such powerful machines. To mitigate this issue, we have introduced a unique method where we do not need a large amount of data for the image processing task. To eliminate the necessity of collecting a huge amount of data, we included a self- enhancing feature, which helps the model to predict accurately and also helps to improve performance by increasing the amount of data.
